big_story.headline: The RBI's Calibrated Tightening Pivot
big_story.subhead: THE RESERVE BANK OF INDIA HIKES THE REPO RATE TO 5.50% TO COMBAT INFLATIONARY PRESSURES
paragraphs: In a significant policy move, the Reserve Bank of India has hiked the repo rate to 5.50% and shifted its stance to calibrated tightening. This decision comes as the central bank navigates growing job complexity and seeks to deliver an adequate response to inflation. Despite the rate hike, the India-US bond yield spread remains near a 22-year low as global yields also adjust.

The pivot highlights the central bank's focus on maintaining fiscal prudence and managing domestic inflation. While the domestic economy has been strengthened by infrastructure investment and reforms, global pressures continue to complicate the monetary landscape. The policy shift aims to anchor inflation expectations while supporting the country's broader economic momentum.

For financial markets, the rate hike introduces a new phase of calibrated tightening that investors must carefully navigate. In today's session so far, the Nifty 50 rose 1.11% to 22,478.30, showing that equity markets are taking the policy tightening in stride. Analysts will be closely watching how the banking sector adapts to these higher borrowing costs in the coming quarters.
big_story.pullbox: The RBI's shift to calibrated tightening and a 5.50% repo rate signals a proactive stance against inflation, even as global bond yield spreads test historic lows.

explains.title: What is Calibrated Tightening?
paragraphs: Calibrated tightening is a monetary policy stance where the central bank signals that it is on a path of raising interest rates, but will do so in a gradual, measured manner. It rules out any rate cuts in the immediate future while keeping the door open for further hikes depending on economic data.

In practice, this stance helps manage inflation expectations without shocking the financial system. By raising the repo rate to 5.50%, the RBI aims to curb excess liquidity and cool down price pressures while ensuring that credit remains available for productive sectors of the economy.

Indian lifestyle and design startup DailyObjects has successfully raised ₹332 crore in its Series C funding round. The funding round was led by private equity firm Xponentia Capital. DailyObjects plans to utilize this capital to fuel its next phase of growth and expand its product portfolio.

This significant capital injection highlights the growing investor confidence in India's consumer brand ecosystem. By securing backing from prominent investors like Xponentia Capital, the startup is well-positioned to scale its operations and strengthen its market presence.

story_1.headline: TCS Q2 Profit Rises 15% to ₹13,884 Crore
paragraphs: Tata Consultancy Services reported a strong performance for the second quarter of FY27, with net profit rising 15% year-on-year to ₹13,884 crore. The IT major's revenue increased by 11.2% during the same period, showcasing resilient growth. Following the earnings announcement, TCS shares jumped 5.46% in today's trading session.

The company's operating margins remained flat, but its artificial intelligence deal flow is slowly picking up. Notably, AI projects have now crossed 10% of the company's topline, marking a significant milestone in its technology pivot.

story_2.headline: India Targets $1 Trillion Exports Despite Weak Outlook
paragraphs: Union Minister Piyush Goyal announced that India is confident of achieving its ambitious target of $1 trillion in exports this fiscal year. Despite a weak global trade outlook and structural challenges, the government expects to sustain economic growth of over 7%.

Speaking at the CII Partnership Summit curtain raiser, Goyal emphasized that India's domestic momentum remains robust. The country is actively pursuing trade agreements, including an upcoming FTA with the European Union expected to be signed in December.

story_3.headline: IT Stocks Propel Sensex and Nifty Rebound
paragraphs: Indian benchmark indices witnessed a strong rebound in today's session, with the Nifty 50 rising 1.11% to 22,478.30 and the Sensex climbing 1.03% to 72,329.88. The rally was primarily driven by major IT stocks like TCS, Infosys, and Tech Mahindra, which surged up to 5% following positive earnings sentiment.

geopolitics.headline: India-EU FTA Set for December Signing, Mid-2027 Rollout
paragraphs: India and the European Union are scheduled to sign a landmark Free Trade Agreement in December. According to EU ambassador Paquet, the trade deal is expected to officially take effect by mid-2027. The agreement represents a key milestone in formalizing economic ties and expanding market opportunities between India and European markets.

While the December signing establishes the formal pact, full implementation will stretch to mid-2027. The timeline gives businesses and exporters lead time to adjust to new trade conditions. Strategic planners will be closely evaluating how the deal impacts long-term investment flows between both regions.
